coupling:
The out-of-bounds write exists only in the composition of the two edited commits; neither diff is unsafe on its own.

Responsibility for the right-edge bound check is split between the commits, and each commit's assumption is correct against the tree as it existed when that commit landed:

* #6251 (3cf1c63, earlier) rewrites edge_sweep_row()'s column walk. In its edited form it drops the per-column window guard `if (cx1 <= col_max)` on the left-to-right branch's final boundary cell and calls cell_add() unconditionally, relying on cell_add()'s own `(unsigned) col >= width` clamp to discard a column that lands one past the surface (col == width). Against the cell_add() that existed at that time (right-bound clamp present), this is behavior-identical: col == width is clamped to a no-op, so this commit alone is benign (verified: PoC clean).

* #6273 (8d1d10b, later) templates cell_add() to add 64-bit scanline accumulators. In its edited form it removes cell_add()'s right-of-surface bound check (`(unsigned) col >= width`), keeping only the col < 0 left-fold, on the stated grounds that edge_sweep_row() already clips the column walk to the visible window since #6251. Against the #6251 that existed at that time (window clipped to col <= width-1, final cell guarded), no caller ever passes col >= width, so this commit alone is benign (verified: PoC clean).

Composed, each commit relies on the other to bound the right edge and neither does: 3cf1c63 passes col == width to cell_add() expecting it to clamp, while 8d1d10b removed exactly that clamp expecting 3cf1c63 to keep col < width. The final boundary cell then writes row_area[width]/row_cover[width] (per-row scratch sized exactly `width`) and sets x_max = width, which makes the subsequent tail `hb_memset(row_buf + x_max + 1, byte, width - 1 - x_max)` underflow to a huge length -> AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow (SIGABRT).

A correct fix must reason across both commits: restoring the bound in only one place (re-adding the final-cell guard in 3cf1c63, OR restoring cell_add()'s right-bound clamp in 8d1d10b) removes the bug, but reviewing either single diff in isolation shows correct, well-motivated maintenance with a locally-valid assumption.
